A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DualToken and retain the same central dual-codebook architecture. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v3's Appendices A–G; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix. Changed experimental settings require qualification but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer evaluations, objective ablations, controlled downstream understanding experiments and generated-image examples in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 reports original understanding and generation results, layer and backbone ablations, quantizer comparisons and computational measurements in the main text and Appendices B–E.

M1.justification: Equation 4 changes semantic supervision from squared L2 distance to squared L2 minus cosine similarity. Appendix C also introduces a variant replacing RVQ with UniTok's MCQ. The central shallow/deep dual-codebook design, separate prediction heads and autoregressive formulation remain intact; expanded projector and training descriptions do not establish additional procedural changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds OCRBench, TextVQA and AI2D to understanding evaluation, including explicit OCR-related coverage. Generation evaluation expands from illustrative examples to GenAI-Bench, MJHQ-30K, GenEval and WISE. Tokenizer training is reported as using CC12M plus ImageNet-1K and 50M LAION-400M images, versus CC12M in v1. The newly disclosed MLLM dataset inventory alone does not establish that those training sources changed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds comparisons with QLIP, UniTok, TokenFlow, Muse-VL and TokLIP, among others, while removing its VQGAN row. The unified-model comparison in Table 5 adds Liquid, TokenFlow, UniTok, UniToken and Show-o2, and removes DreamLLM and SEEDLLaMA. The combined SigLIP/MoVQGAN baseline already existed in v1 and is not a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: v1 specifies 384px inputs, SigLIP-SO400M and residual depth 8; v3 includes 256px/depth-4 and 384px/depth-8 configurations, additional backbones and 7B models. Table 4 switches from SigLIP-SO400M/384 to SigLIP-L/256 and normalizes MME scores. New generation experiments introduce VQAScore/FID protocols and a matched Qwen2.5-3B VILA-U reproduction. Appendix B adds controlled backbone/layer experiments with fixed quantization settings and 2M training samples.

E4.justification: v3 adds pixel-only generation ablations, inter-layer similarity and clustering analyses, UMAP comparisons, reconstruction-layer sensitivity across backbones and model sizes, RVQ-versus-MCQ experiments, and computational-cost analysis. It also quantifies the previously qualitative dual-encoder comparison on MJHQ-30K. These substantially extend the questions tested beyond v1's objective ablation and semantic-only understanding comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's dataset-averaged similarities and computational measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the SigLIP-SO400M DualToken results, including rFID 0.54 to 0.25 and zero-shot accuracy 81.6 to 82.0, under changed training and loss settings. v3 newly reports GenAI-Bench scores of 0.68 versus 0.55 for pixel-only generation, and MJHQ-30K FID of 7.88 versus 17.55 for the dual encoder. Numerous configuration and appendix results are added. The original Table 5 score vector is retained but labeled 256px despite v1's stated 384px setup, preventing an unqualified same-setting comparison.

T1.justification: Equation 4 substantively revises the mathematical definition of the semantic loss by adding negative cosine similarity. The other central quantization and autoregressive equations remain equivalent. No theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The core conflict-resolution contribution remains, but v3 adds a claim of using only 10% of VILA-U's tokenizer-pretraining data and elevates reciprocal benefits of pixel and semantic tokens to a main finding. Its conclusion claims state-of-the-art unified-model performance among discrete autoregressive approaches and a first demonstration of hierarchical conflict resolution. v1 presents the downstream model more cautiously as a baseline implementation with further task synergy left to explore.

C2.justification: v3 newly attributes dual-encoder degradation to incompatible representation spaces, explains pixel-token benefits as compensation for quantization-related semantic loss, and interprets semantic tokens as supervision for generation. Appendices B–D discuss layer-selection generality, complementarity with MCQ and computational overhead. Conversely, Section 3.2 softens v1's claim that semantic supervision improves reconstruction to saying it does not degrade reconstruction.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents four-stage MLLM training, learning rates, batch sizes and optimizers in Table 13, and stage-specific datasets in Table 14. Appendix F supplies projector architecture, image-boundary tokens, clustering/UMAP procedures and detailed dual-encoder implementation controls. It also adds a project-page link and states that clustering code accompanies supplementary material, without establishing availability from these PDFs alone. However, v1's EMA/codebook-restart description and CFG value of 3 are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around newer unified tokenizers and dual-encoder systems, including FQGAN, UniTok, QLIP, TokLIP and ILLUME+. Appendix C explicitly positions DualToken's hierarchical design as complementary to UniTok's quantizer improvements. The v1 assertion that TokenFlow lacks a unified understanding-and-generation model disappears. These are substantive changes beyond reference-format and publication-status updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around explicit findings and updated positioning. Experiments are reorganized into tokenizer and unified-model sections, while implementation material is expanded and partly relocated to dedicated appendices. Terminology is refined toward pixel/appearance and semantic vocabularies, and author, affiliation and conference-header information changes.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, expands Figure 1, and redraws v1's Figure 3 as Figure 4. The generation gallery becomes a structured comparison with VILA-U and pixel-only outputs. New similarity, clustering and UMAP figures accompany substantially expanded tables, including a two-part Table 5 and appendix Tables 7–14.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's reliance on qualitative generation examples and sparse implementation reporting. Quantitative generation benchmarks, matched comparisons, token ablations, cross-backbone layer tests and detailed training documentation provide much stronger support for the central design. Lost EMA/CFG details, absent uncertainty estimates and inconsistent resolution labeling remain limitations, and higher cross-version scores cannot be attributed solely to the method. Nevertheless, the added controlled evidence and reproducibility information resolve important weaknesses and clearly improve overall quality.
